questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the diameter of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror?

questions.stem: A convex lens forms a real, inverted and enlarged image of an object. Where is the object most likely placed?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Between F and 2F'. When an object is placed between the focal point and twice the focal length of a convex lens, the lens forms a real, inverted, and enlarged image. If the object is at infinity, the image is tiny and formed at the focal point. If the object is at twice the focal length, the image is the same size as the object. If the object is between the focal point and the lens, the image is virtual and upright.

questions.stem: A light ray travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium. What happens to the light ray?
choices: It bends away from the normal
It continues in a straight line
questions.solution: When a light ray travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it bends towards the normal. This is a fundamental law of refraction. The options 'It reflects back' and 'It continues in a straight line' are incorrect as they do not describe the behavior of refraction.

The refraction at both surfaces is equal and opposite
The light ray is not affected by the glass slab
The glass slab is too thin to affect the direction of the light ray
questions.solution: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray because the refraction at both surfaces is equal and opposite. At the first surface, the light bends towards the normal, and at the second surface, it bends away from the normal, resulting in the emergent ray being parallel. The other options are incorrect because the angles are not equal, the glass slab does affect the direction, and the thickness is not the reason for the parallelism.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the central point of a lens?
questions.solution: The term used to describe the central point of a lens is the optical centre, which is the point through which light rays pass undeviated. questions.stem: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted, and highly diminished image of an object. Where is the object located?
choices: Between the focus and the centre of curvature
questions.solution: The image formed by a concave mirror is real, inverted, and highly diminished when the object is placed at infinity. This is because the parallel rays coming from a distant object converge at the focus after reflection, forming a point-sized image. The other options do not result in a highly diminished image. Placing the object at the focus would result in an image at infinity, at the centre of curvature would form an image of the same size, and between the focus and the centre of curvature would form an enlarged image.

questions.stem: A student draws a ray diagram for a concave mirror. One ray is drawn from the object through the principal focus of the mirror. What happens to this ray after reflection?
choices: It is reflected back along the same path
It is reflected parallel to the principal axis
It is reflected at an angle equal to the angle of incidence
It is reflected in a random direction
questions.solution: The ray passing through the principal focus of a concave mirror is reflected parallel to the principal axis. This is a standard rule for ray diagrams of concave mirrors. The other options are incorrect because: (1) A ray reflected back along the same path would only happen if it was incident along the normal, (2) The angle of incidence is not directly mentioned in the rule, and (3) the ray does not reflect randomly.
